title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-Live Planning
next_steps: Provision additional GPU capacity on Dedicated by 2027-01-20
Share SOC2 + network diagrams and KMS notes
action_items: Alex Morgan | Send pricing + final SOC2 docs | 2027-01-15
Priya Shah | Prepare canary test plan + A/B metric definitions | 2027-01-18
Sara Kim | Validate VPC peering config in staging and report issues | 2027-01-20
Jamal Bryant | Finalize success criteria (p95 latency, error budget) | 2027-01-18
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on rollout plan: canary/A-B strategy, cutover steps, monitoring and runbooks. Agreement on success criteria, next steps to finalize runbook and schedule canary, and action items assigned for docs, capacity, and network validation.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here. Quick check — can you hear me?
[00:04] Jamal Bryant: Yep, loud and clear. Jamal on my side.
[00:07] Sara Kim: Sara, good morning.
[00:09] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood SE. I shared the staging runbook link in the chat, hopefully you all got it.
[00:15] Luis Ortega: Got it. Will review after call.
[00:17] Alex Morgan: Great. Agenda for today: run through the rollout/cutover plan, discuss canary and A/B strategy, monitoring and alerts, and finalize next steps. We have about 55 minutes.
[00:30] Jamal Bryant: Sounds good. Last week we agreed on baseline metrics; we've run additional load tests overnight. Priya, do you want to start with results?
[00:38] Priya Shah: Sure. Quick caveat — transcription may mix up some numbers — but from staging runs: median latency for the Redwood Dedicated instance at 512 tokens was ~120ms, p95 is ~340ms under our synthetic traffic. Under the mixed-batch realistic workload — which includes prefix caching — we saw p95 dip to ~280ms. So that looks promising.
[01:05] Jamal Bryant: Okay, 280–340 p95 range. That's within our target? We set p95 < 400ms for the pilot.
[01:12] Alex Morgan: Right, target is p95 < 400ms, and error rate below 0.5% per 10k requests. Also cost per 1k tokens target we discussed.
[01:22] Sara Kim: On errors we saw some occasional timeouts when we pushed concurrency to simulate spikes — I think that was due to insufficient autoscale headroom on the staging Dedicated pool.
[01:33] Priya Shah: Yeah, that matches logs — we saw queue growth in the scheduler for brief periods. For production we recommend configuring burst capacity plus the fast fallback policy to hosted variants if Dedicated saturation occurs.
[01:45] Jamal Bryant: We prefer to avoid fallback to hosted for data residency reasons — some requests contain PII we can't send to hosted. Is there a way to keep it within Private/VPC?
[01:56] Priya Shah: Absolutely — for Private deployments you can configure region pinning and no-hosted fallback. For this POC your plan is Dedicated in your cloud account with VPC peering, correct?
[02:06] Sara Kim: Correct — Dedicated with VPC peering into our AWS account. We're using customer-managed KMS, per the security review.
[02:14] Alex Morgan: Good. That means fallback isn't allowed, so autoscaling and capacity planning are critical. On that note, we recommend the initial Dedicated pool be provisioned at 1.5x the steady-state predicted QPS to cover spikes during cutover.
[02:27] Jamal Bryant: Can you quantify that in GPUs? Right now staging used two p4d equivalents — for production what do you think?
[02:34] Priya Shah: For your query mix and expected traffic, I'd suggest starting with four cards and enabling rapid autoscale to eight for burst. Also consider model quantization we tested — the INT8 profile reduced average latency by ~15% and halves memory, letting more instances run per GPU.
[02:50] Luis Ortega: Quick security question — the SOC2 artefacts you sent, does Redwood rotate keys or is that customer-managed? We want audit logs for KMS usage.
[02:58] Alex Morgan: Keys are customer-managed for Private/Dedicated with KMS integration; Redwood logs KMS calls in the audit trail but does not hold keys. We'll share the SOC2 network diagrams and KMS notes in the drive.
[03:10] Sara Kim: Please do. Also we need to confirm SSO + RBAC mapping before cutover.
[03:15] Alex Morgan: Agreed, that's part of the go-live checklist. I'll include the SSO mapping steps in the runbook.
[03:20] Priya Shah: Back to cutover — propose a three-stage plan: 1) Dry run in staging (done), 2) Canary in production at 5% traffic for 48 hours with golden metrics, 3) Gradual ramp to 100% with A/B checks and rollback gates.
[03:34] Jamal Bryant: 5% for 48 hours — ok. For the canary we'll need a control traffic pool and a way to route by header or cookie. Our prod gateway can do weighted routing.
[03:44] Priya Shah: Perfect. For A/B metrics we want to observe: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost, and qualitative NLU quality checks — we'll tie that to a small eval prompt set that you ran last week.
[03:58] Jamal Bryant: On the eval set — we saw a small regression on the payments terms detection on the new quantized variant. It was like 2% drop. Is that expected?
[04:06] Priya Shah: That's plausible; quantization sometimes affects subtle classification. We can run the eval suite in the canary and if regression >1% we'll prevent ramp. The Optimize recommendations included a lighter quant profile that keeps accuracy but still gives cost wins.
[04:19] Alex Morgan: We'll codify that as a gate: canary passes if regression <1% on the eval set AND p95 < 400ms AND error <0.5%.
[04:28] Sara Kim: Monitoring — we want to integrate Redwood metrics into our Datadog. How granular are the traces and logs?
[04:35] Priya Shah: We stream per-route latency histograms, tokens per request, model variant, and per-token cost. We can push metrics to Datadog via our exporter or via Prometheus. Traces are supported too; we'll share the template dashboards.
[04:47] Luis Ortega: Alerts — we need an alert for sustained p95 > 450ms and an alert for error rate spikes. Also an SRE on-call runbook for rollback.
[04:56] Alex Morgan: Our default runbook includes automated rollback to previous model variant if canary error budget is exceeded. We'll include playbooks: scope, rollback command, who to call. Priya, you had a note on rollback commands.
[05:07] Priya Shah: Yep, the CLI command is in the runbook — 'redwood rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <ver>' — but in your Private setup it maps to a managed API call. We'll include exact IAM roles needed.
[05:18] Jamal Bryant: For the cutover day, who will be the owner? We need someone from Redwood to be oncall and someone from Acme.
[05:25] Alex Morgan: Redwood owner for cutover will be me (Alex) and Priya will be SE on standby. Customer owner? Jamal, are you OK being primary?
[05:33] Jamal Bryant: I can be primary, Sara will be network owner. Luis will own security checks.
[05:37] Alex Morgan: Great. We'll put that in the runbook.
[05:40] Sara Kim: One more network thing — during staging we noticed a 30s delay for the first request after VPC cold path — NAT gateway warm-up maybe. Any mitigation?
[05:48] Priya Shah: That sounds like ENI warm-up coupled with cold model load. We recommend a health-warmup hook — the canary plan includes a pre-warm phase that sends low-frequency ping requests to keep endpoints warm. We'll add that to the cutover timeline.
[05:59] Jamal Bryant: Timeline — we want go-live before end of month. Is 2027-01-28 still realistic for canary?
[06:04] Alex Morgan: Yes, 2027-01-28 for canary start. That gives two weeks to finalize docs and provisioning. Full ramp could be 2027-02-03 if canary passes.
[06:12] Jamal Bryant: Ok. Regarding cost — can you send updated pricing if we commit to reserved capacity for three months?
[06:17] Alex Morgan: I'll put a reserved capacity quote in the follow-up. There is a committed discount; I'll include both burst and reserved options.
[06:24] Sara Kim: On compliance, we still need the DPA and updated SOC2 attestation for the Private deployment.
[06:29] Alex Morgan: We'll share the DPA and SOC2 PDF today. Also the network diagrams and KMS notes.
[06:34] Luis Ortega: Good. For audit logs, can we get a sample log line format?
[06:38] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll attach sample audit logs. They include timestamp, request id, model version, user id hash, and KMS operation id.
[06:46] Jamal Bryant: Switching to A/B specifics — when we ramp to 50/50 A/B, do we plan to run both models in parallel on separate pools or on same deployment with version flag?
[06:56] Priya Shah: For isolation we recommend separate deployment groups — that way you can isolate resource pressure. Your gateway will weight traffic. If resource utilization is fine, we can then collapse to a single deployment with version flag.
[07:07] Sara Kim: Ok. Also need to measure cost delta between variants — can Redwood annotate per-request token cost in the header so we can compute delta?
[07:14] Priya Shah: Yes, we can surface per-request cost via response metadata or via metrics export. We'll enable that for the canary.
[07:21] Alex Morgan: Quick note on SLO burn — we'll run a canary script that simulates user sessions and records the key metrics to Datadog so alerts are meaningful.
[07:30] Jamal Bryant: Back to runbook items — what are the rollback decision points? You said regressions >1% or p95 violation? Need to formalize.
[07:39] Priya Shah: We'll include a decision tree: 1) Eval regression >1% -> immediate stop and rollback. 2) p95 > 400ms sustained for 10 minutes -> investigate; if no mitigation in 15 minutes, rollback. 3) Error rate spike >0.5% on 10k window -> rollback. 4) Any security incident -> immediate rollback.
[07:57] Sara Kim: How fast is rollback? Seconds, minutes?
[08:00] Priya Shah: In most cases rollback is near-instant once you flip routing — propagation depends on your gateway (usually under a minute). Warmup may take a couple minutes; we'll include traffic shaping to minimize disruption.
[08:11] Jamal Bryant: For the canary duration — 48 hours seems long. Can we do 24h if all gates pass?
[08:16] Alex Morgan: We can — 48h is conservative. Let's set initial plan at 48h but allow compress to 24h if all automated gates and spot checks pass and no anomalies. We'll document criteria for compressing.
[08:26] Luis Ortega: On the topic of logs retention, how long do we keep request logs in Redwood? We need 90 days for the audit.
[08:33] Alex Morgan: For Private + Dedicated, you set retention; Redwood can push logs to your account's S3/Cloud Storage. We'll include the retention configuration in the runbook.
[08:43] Jamal Bryant: Excellent. Anything else from Redwood side?
[08:46] Priya Shah: I'll take the canary test plan and metric definitions offline and post in the shared drive by 2027-01-18.
[08:54] Alex Morgan: I'll send the runbook draft and pricing by 2027-01-15 and the SOC2 + DPA docs today. Also we'll request confirmation of cutover owners.
[09:03] Sara Kim: We'll validate VPC peering and NAT behavior by 2027-01-20 and let you know if any changes needed.
[09:10] Jamal Bryant: Ok let's call out the next meeting — propose 2027-01-21 to finalize the runbook and confirm provisioning.
[09:16] Alex Morgan: Works for us, I'll send the calendar invite.
[09:19] Luis Ortega: Quick note — please include phone numbers for escalation in the runbook; emails are fine but we want on-call numbers.
[09:25] Alex Morgan: Will do.
[09:27] Jamal Bryant: Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Priya Shah: Thanks — see you on the 21st.
[09:30] Alex Morgan: End.

Notes: transcription includes filler and occasional mis-heard terms; specific numbers should be validated against raw logs. Shared artifacts: Drive: Runbook draft (link), SOC2 attestation (link), Reserved capacity quote (link), Canary test plan (link).

End of transcript.
